title: Caution — while θεόπνευστοι still spoke, written Scripture was not yet the full deposit
source_text: XXX. Id tamen intelligendum videtur cum hac cautione, nempe sublatis viris θεοπνεύστοις per quos crevit divinae revelationis lumen, & editis eorum scriptis. Ut excipiatur tempus quo viva vox eorum in Ecclesia resonabat, nec dum scriptis consignaverant quae Deo placitum erat de novo ipsis revelare. Nam, exempli gratia, quum Apostoli praedicare coeperunt, neque adhuc quicquam scripserant, Scriptura veteris Testamenti non continebat omnia ad salutem necessaria, nisi confuse & implicite, quatenus nos ad verum Messiam remittebat, a quo plenius de Dei voluntate edoceremur.
pass_a_gloss: Yet that seems to be understood with this caution, namely with the θεοπνεύστοις men removed through whom the light of divine revelation grew, and with their writings published. So that the time is excepted when their living voice still sounded in the Church, and they had not yet consigned in writings the things it pleased God to reveal to them anew. For, for example, when the Apostles began to preach, and had not yet written anything, the Scripture of the Old Testament did not contain all things necessary to salvation except confusedly and implicitly, insofar as it remitted us to the true Messiah, from whom we should be more fully taught concerning the will of God.
pass_b_english: Take that with this caution: once the θεόπνευστοι men through whom revelation's light grew are gone, and their writings are out.

Except the time when their living voice still sounded in the Church, before they had put in writing what God was pleased to reveal to them anew. For example, when the Apostles began to preach and had not yet written anything, Old Testament Scripture did not hold all needful for salvation except in a mixed, implicit way — inasmuch as it sent us to the true Messiah, from whom we would be taught God's will more fully.

choices.why: Ablative absolute: after their removal, once writings published.
